story.title: Four Cedis in a Hundred
story.angle: Agriculture is the backbone of jobs (37%) and output (23%), but just over 4 cedis in every 100 of bank loans — even in a year it outgrew the economy
story.editorial_decision: Final video delivered and approved by GilB on 2026-11-25 ("completed"). Not yet published. Stage held at Review because the registry only allows Ready to publish once every claim is Verified; 7 of 9 claims await the research-pack open checks.
story.claim_confidence: Jobs figures verified in the GSS report; GDP figures as reported from the GSS release; BoG credit shares read from report chart labels. Open checks recorded in the research pack and issues.
story.next_action: Complete the research-pack open checks (BoG data table, GSS release) and mark claims Verified; then Ready to publish, publish and record post URLs.

analyses.question: Is agriculture the backbone of Ghana's economy — by jobs, by output and by bank loans?
analyses.approach: Three shares for the same year (2025): employment (GSS QLFS Q3 2025), GDP (GSS 2025 release) and bank credit outstanding (BoG MPR Jan 2026). Growth comparison from the GSS release; agriculture's cedi amount computed as share × gross loans, with a rounding-band check.
analyses.finding: Agriculture is 37.2% of jobs and 22.8% of output but 4.3% of banks' outstanding loans (Dec 2025). Agriculture grew 6.8% vs 6.0% for the economy; bank loans to agriculture rose ≈ +6% while all bank loans rose 16.2%, so the share fell from 4.7% to 4.3%.
analyses.peer_check: Research pack consolidated 2026-11-25; owner delivered final video as completed 2026-11-25
analyses.limitations: BoG shares read from chart labels; GDP share and growth taken from a press report of the GSS release; bank loans cover deposit money banks only. Bad-loan ratios, causes, targets, June 2026 data and GIRSAL researched but deliberately left out (research pack §6–7).

evidence.claim: Out of every hundred working Ghanaians, about thirty-seven work in agriculture.
evidence.qualification: 37.2% of employed persons aged 15+, Q3 2025 (GSS QLFS).
About 5.0 million employed in agriculture, Q3 2025 (GSS QLFS).

evidence.claim: Out of every hundred cedis of economic output produced in 2025, about twenty-three came from agriculture.
evidence.verification_status: Reported by GSS (via GNA); release not yet checked directly
evidence.qualification: 22.8% of GDP, 2025 provisional. Real vs nominal share still to confirm in the GSS release.

evidence.claim: At the end of 2025, out of every hundred cedis Ghana's banks had outstanding in loans, just over four cedis were in agriculture.
evidence.verification_status: Chart reading; BoG data table not yet checked
evidence.qualification: 4.3% of total bank credit outstanding, Dec 2025 (BoG MPR Jan 2026, Fig 6.1). Total credit, not private-sector credit (4.5%), not new-lending flows.

evidence.claim: In 2025, agriculture grew by 6.8 percent, faster than the economy's overall growth of 6 percent.
evidence.verification_status: Reported by GSS (via GNA); release not yet checked directly

evidence.claim: Bank loans to agriculture actually went up.
evidence.qualification: ≈ GH¢4.49bn (Dec 2024) → ≈ GH¢4.77bn (Dec 2025), ≈ +6%; share × gross loans. Direction holds across the shares' rounding bands (+4% to +9%).

evidence.claim: But bank loans overall went up faster.
evidence.qualification: Gross loans GH¢111.0bn at Dec 2025, +16.2% y/y.

evidence.claim: So agriculture's share fell, from 4.7 percent to 4.3 percent.
evidence.verification_status: Chart reading; BoG data table not yet checked
evidence.qualification: Dec 2024 → Dec 2025, share of total bank credit outstanding.

evidence.claim: Now, these are bank loans, not every source of financing agriculture relies on.
evidence.qualification: BoG figures cover deposit money banks only; rural/community banks, microfinance, input credit and outgrower schemes are outside the measure.
